novelty_flags.label: prop:sharp-score-reduction
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed sharp p=2 score/endpoints reduction is Watson et al.'s published Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7, so it cannot be presented as a novel root result.

soundness_flags.label: ass:treatment-orthogonality
soundness_flags.one_line: Because beta(P)=Sigma_zz(P)^(-1)Sigma_zx(P), the treatment equation X=beta(P)'Z+epsilon_x already implies E[Z epsilon_x]=0; retain one formulation, not both.

soundness_flags.label: thm:minimax-loss-frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: The interior clause says only that an unspecified Gaussian path yields an 'analogous lower rate' without stating the coverage class, loss inequality, constants, or verified membership in P^int(delta_0).

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:adaptive-score-hull and thm:minimax-loss-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Uniform coverage and the matched upper frontier are conditional on an affirmative resolution of oeq:uniform-multiplier-coupling, including uniform integrability of the score-band radius.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The multiplier-hull coverage and upper loss rates are claimed conditional on the stated uniform multiplier coupling; the Gaussian lower bounds remain separate targets.

source_verification_receipts.locator: PDF p. 5, Corollary 2.1; PDF p. 17, Appendix A.7; PDF p. 6, Theorem 4; PDF p. 19, Appendix A.9
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Corollary 2.1 gives the closed-form scalar-L2 sharp endpoints; Appendix A.7 derives them from a quadratic leakage equation. Theorem 4 retains only feasible bootstrap draws, and Appendix A.9 calls the optimizer differentiable and conditions its sampling distribution on feasibility.
The cited publication is the boundary-bootstrap inconsistency paper; it is an adjacent generic comparator rather than a leaky-IV result.
The paper establishes that full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for standard-bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian first-stage limit and proposes an alternative resampling scheme.
The paper constructs random sets covering identified sets and gives conditions for uniform-in-P validity.
The paper obtains bootstrap critical values uniformly approximating a subset of a local parameter space for constrained conditional-moment models.
The paper gives Gaussian approximation and conditional Gaussian-multiplier bootstrap approximation for maxima of sums of high-dimensional random vectors.
The paper proves nonexistence of locally asymptotically unbiased or alpha-quantile-unbiased estimators for nondifferentiable targets; it does not give the proposed leaky-IV set-loss rate.

The numerical bootstrap paper covers fixed and drifting nonregular sequences and discusses partially identified-model test statistics, but does not state the proposed unknown-index leaky-IV retained-kernel result.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference 236, 2025, article 106245
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Li gives uniformly valid inference for root-n consistent constrained optimization estimators including sequences drifting to a boundary; this does not subsume a fourth-root partially identified interval endpoint.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the interior sentence in thm:minimax-loss-frontier with a complete quantified lower-bound display, including the exact coverage condition, directed-loss functional, compact t-set, and class-compatibility inequalities.
Delete ass:treatment-orthogonality or define beta as a free structural coefficient rather than the covariance projection, then state the remaining orthogonality condition only once.

Make the contact nonuniformity theorem report a direct limiting percentile-coverage calculation for a specified h-region, rather than relying on bounded-Lipschitz separation as the sole bridge to coverage failure.

Prove the finite-dimensional conditional multiplier approximation directly from the quadratic coefficient vector and give an explicit uniform-integrability bound; this resolves the sole load-bearing OEQ and converts the conditional hull result into the field-level contribution.

recommended_next_step: Continue revision on this angle: remove the known Watson reduction from the novelty kernel, make the interior minimax lower bound fully quantified, and then pursue the explicit multiplier-coupling proof.
